Distribute food equally to all refugees without exclusion or diversion to guards
Hand food over for guards to organize and carry out distribution
Grant FWB staff case-by-case access to additional blocks beyond the escort routine

Involve MASHA and local actors in distribution inside the camp

goals.label: Accurate nutritional data and documentation for accountability to donors
Outsiders move freely in the camp and hostile actors exploit that access
Aid food is diverted, skimmed or seized by guards or authorities
Camp power and security infrastructure keep running
Commander's authority and image of strength with guards and militia
Control over information, influence and the narrative about the camp
FWB staff have independent access and movement inside the camp
FWB's neutrality, with aid not feeding or paying armed guards
Food reaches all refugees equally, with no groups excluded
Food remains usable as currency in the camp
Guards and militia control food distribution
Guards and their families are fed and compensated, keeping guards loyal
Host town's economy and goodwill, with local actors prioritized
Ongoing supply of food aid into the camp
Refugees stay contained in the camp, away from the capital
Aid food is traded or resold rather than eaten by refugees
Backing from the militia leadership and government
Distribution follows FWB's humanitarian procedures and standards
Refugees face abuse or collective punishment linked to food
Refugees receive enough food to meet their needs
Working relationship with local partner MASHA

redLines.label: Allow FWB and its chosen local assistants to manage food disbursement directly
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Manage food disbursement directly with FWB staff and FWB-chosen local assistants
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Provide food rations or compensation to guards and their families
redLines.quote: If they see the refugees eating better than they are, they may well rebel, and it may be your head. Or someone in your family's head.

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
